subject: Recap: Slop Code Bench & AI's Evolving Code Quality
body:
Hello First Name,

Our latest 🦄 ai that works session was all about "Slop Code Bench" and diving into AI's emergent coding behaviors!

If you missed it, or want to revisit anything, the full recording, code, and diagrams are now available on GitHub:
https://github.com/hellovai/ai-that-works

We dug into some interesting insights from Slop Code Bench and how AI-generated code quality is changing. Here's what we talked about:

*   **Slop is evolving, not disappearing.** While models are getting better, new, more subtle, and dangerous issues are popping up. These aren't just individual bad lines anymore; they're moving into dependencies and error handling, replacing older patterns like `sys.exit`.
*   **Agents often rewrite libraries from scratch.** They seem reluctant to use existing ones. Even when they design new libraries, they copy human-preferred structures but don't optimize for how agents would actually use them, like preferring runnable examples over traditional documentation.
*   **Complex problems still stump models.** For moderately complex problems (think 10-20k lines of code), models struggle with good design patterns. This hurts maintainability and pushes the dream of fully autonomous "dark factory" software development further away.

If there's one key takeaway from the session, it's this: AI-generated code isn't just about a few bad lines anymore. The "slop" is becoming more systemic and harder to spot. This really impacts maintainability and makes fully autonomous agent development tougher, meaning we need to rethink how we judge code quality.

Got questions? Just hit reply or jump into our Discord: https://www.boundaryml.com/discord. We're always happy to chat! Happy coding 🧑‍💻

Vaibhav & Dex
